Issued at 327 PM EDT Fri Oct 30 2026

Friday Afternoon - Saturday Night...

Broad upper level ridging is in place over the Southeast and Ohio 
Valley this afternoon, with sfc high pressure over Lake Michigan. A 
weak cold front has pushed into south-central KY, with much drier 
air (30s/40s dewpoints) to the north of the boundary across north-
central KY. Drier low-level air will continue to filter in from the 
northeast this evening as high pressure builds southeast over the 
Great Lakes. The weather will remain very pleasant through this 
evening, with only scattered, thin high clouds. Current temperatures 
range from the lower 70s in the Bluegrass to the upper 70s/near 80 
in southern KY. Temperatures will likely rise at least another 
degree or two over the next 2-3 hours before steadily falling this 
evening. Temperatures will drop through the 60s and 50s between 8-10 
PM. 

After sunset, we'll see increasing high clouds ahead of an upper 
level shortwave trough lifting northeast out of the southern Plains. 
High clouds will become overcast on Halloween, but we'll stay dry 
thanks to much drier air in the lower levels. High pressure will 
remain anchored over the Appalachians, providing a drying influence. 
However, we do start to see northward moisture return up the Lower 
MS Valley on the western periphery of the low-level ridge. 

Overall, expect a mostly cloudy Halloween with highs in the 70s. 
Temperatures will dip into the 60s shortly after sunset. Steady 
moisture return continues Saturday night ahead of a compact 
mid/upper level wave. Top-down saturation should be quick enough to 
yield measurable light rainfall across the SW CWA prior to 12Z 
Sunday (7 AM EST). Lows Sunday morning are expected to reach the mid 
50s.  

Sunday - Monday Night...

The compact mid/upper level trough, positioned just downstream of an 
amplifying ridge over the Plains, will cross the Lower OH Valley on 
Sunday. Strong low-level ridging will remain anchored over the Mid-
Atlantic, and a notable west-to-east moisture gradient is 
anticipated across KY. A 25-30+ kt SSE LLJ will produce stronger 
moisture transport up through Middle TN and west-central KY. As 
such, we still expect higher rainfall amounts along and west of the 
I-65 corridor through the weekend. Current expected rainfall amounts 
through the weekend range from less than 0.10" in the Bluegrass to 
0.50-0.75" in our SW and west-central KY counties. Drier air to the 
east should really eat into rainfall amounts, and areas east of I-75 
may be lucky to see measurable rainfall. 

The upper level shortwave disturbance exits off to the east Sunday 
night, with an upper level ridge building in on Monday. A deepening 
upper level trough and sfc low are forecast to develop over the 
central Plains on Monday. The model trend is for a dry day across 
central KY and southern IN. We should stay dry through at least 
Monday night as well, with the Plains system occluding and slowing 
down. 

Tuesday - Friday...

Notably stronger northward moisture transport takes place Tuesday 
into Wednesday ahead of the stacked low pressure system over the 
Midwest. A band of moderate to heavy rain showers appears possible, 
and the mostly likely timing is currently late Tuesday night through 
Wednesday, perhaps lingering into Wednesday night. Breezy southerly 
winds will also accompany this frontal passage during the midweek 
time frame. The risk for severe storms looks quite low at this time 
due to limited instability. It appears the higher risk for strong to 
severe storms will be down across the Lower MS Valley. 

Given the ongoing drought conditions, the risk for significant 
flooding is low. However, a round of heavier showers could certainly 
cause some ponding on roads on Wednesday. Drier conditions are 
anticipated late next week in the wake of the cold frontal passage.
